Summarize a fitted semi-parametric Hawkes model

Source: R/fit_semihawkes.R
summary.semihawkes_fit.Rd

Reports what the print() method does not: the study window the model was fitted over, the estimated branching structure (how the observed events divide between background and triggered), the range of each fitted background component, and how the EM run terminated.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'semihawkes_fit'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.semihawkes_fit'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

A semihawkes_fit object from fit_semihawkes().

...

Currently unused.

x

A summary.semihawkes_fit object.

Value

An object of class "summary.semihawkes_fit", a list with elements n_events, start_date, end_date, TT, crs, mu, A, llik, triggered_share, background_share, n_background, n_triggered, components (a data.frame of per-component ranges), n_iter, stop_reason and llik_change. Printed by print.summary.semihawkes_fit().

Interpreting A

Because g and h are each normalized to integrate to 1, the branching ratio A is the expected number of direct offspring generated by each event. For a subcritical process (A < 1) it is also the long-run proportion of events that are offspring rather than immigrants, so it can be read directly as a triggered share. The empirical counterpart reported alongside it is 1 - mean(bgprobs), the average fitted probability that an observed event was triggered; the two agree when the model fits well and the window is long relative to the triggering range.

Examples

# \donttest{
# A quick fit to one year of the bundled simulated data: a coarse grid, a
# coarse triggering-kernel grid and two EM iterations keep it to a few
# seconds. Real analyses need finer settings and more iterations.
cache_dir <- tempfile("spHawkes_marks_")
fit <- fit_semihawkes(
  sim_events, sim_region,
  date_col  = "date",
  end_date  = "2022-01-01",
  cell_size = 1000,
  cache_dir = cache_dir,
  trigger_spatial_args = list(x_range = 2000, x_step = 250),
  trigger_window_dist  = 2000,
  n_iter  = 2,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed    = 1
)
#> The modelled study period ends on 2021-12-29, the day after the last event. `end_date` (2022-01-01) is used only to select events and to label outputs.
summary(fit)
#> Semi-parametric spatio-temporal Hawkes fit
#> ------------------------------------------------------------
#> Events        : 98
#> Study window  : 2021-01-03 to 2022-01-01 (modelled to 2021-12-29, 360 days)
#> CRS           : EPSG:32717
#> 
#> Parameters
#>   mu (baseline rate)     : 2.59201e-09  per unit area per day
#>   A  (branching ratio)   : 0.5504  expected offspring per event
#>   log-likelihood         : -1875.36
#> 
#> Branching structure (from fitted background probabilities)
#>   background :     57.5 events ( 58.7%)
#>   triggered  :     40.5 events ( 41.3%)
#> 
#> Fitted components (range over their support)
#>   trend               [    0.7379,      1.138]
#>   weekly              [    0.6428,      1.494]
#>   monthly             [    0.5821,      1.274]
#>   spatial background  [  0.005398,      5.897]
#>   trigger (temporal)  [  0.001207,    0.07197]
#>   trigger (spatial)   [         0,  7.789e-07]
#> 
#> Convergence
#>   2 EM iterations, reached n_iter without converging
#>   final change in log-likelihood: 7.87588
# }
